q: The alkanes are the simplest family of organic compounds and are referred to as the '____ hydrocarbons'.
e: The alkanes are the simplest family of organic compounds and are referred to as the 'saturated hydrocarbons'. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

q: Alkanes contain only ____ and hydrogen atoms.
e: Alkanes contain only carbon and hydrogen atoms. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. Organic chemistry is built on carbon-hydrogen frameworks with covalent bonds.

q: Every carbon in an alkane has a ____ environment and is bonded to four other atoms.
e: Every carbon in an alkane has a tetrahedral environment and is bonded to four other atoms. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2.

q: Alkanes form a homologous series, with the general formula ____ where n is a number equal to or greater than 1.
e: Alkanes form a homologous series, with the general formula C_nH2n+2 where n is a number equal to or greater than 1. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once.

e: The representative alkane given here is ethane, C_2H_6. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2.

q: Two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms and have different properties from each other are called ____.
e: Two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms and have different properties from each other are called isomers. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ. The molecular formula gives the actual number of each kind of atom in one molecule.

q: Straight chain and branched-chain isomers are examples of ____ isomers that differ in the order in which the atoms are bonded together.
e: Straight chain and branched-chain isomers are examples of structural isomers that differ in the order in which the atoms are bonded together. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ.

q: All of the alkanes containing ____ or more carbon atoms show structural isomerism.

q: In the laboratory, alkanes are prepared by heating the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with ____.
e: In the laboratory, alkanes are prepared by heating the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with soda lime. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. A carboxylic acid has the -COOH group, which makes the molecule acidic.

q: Soda lime is a mixture of ____ (lime) and sodium hydroxide.
e: Soda lime is a mixture of calcium oxide (lime) and sodium hydroxide. Lime is a mixture of lime and sodium.

q: The reduction of alkyl halides with molecular hydrogen takes place in the presence of catalyst like platinum, Pt or ____, Pd.
e: The reduction of alkyl halides with molecular hydrogen takes place in the presence of catalyst like platinum, Pt or palladium, Pd. A catalyst speeds a reaction by lowering activation energy and is not used up in the overall change.

q: The alkanes are ____ toward acids, bases, metals and many other chemicals.

q: Alkanes burn well in a good supply of oxygen, forming ____ and water vapour, and giving out plenty of heat.
e: Alkanes burn well in a good supply of oxygen, forming carbon dioxide and water vapour, and giving out plenty of heat. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2.

q: If there is not enough oxygen, the alkanes undergo incomplete combustion, giving off poisonous ____ and less heat energy.
